question: Which selling rule grows the approved $100k account best after risk over twenty years, and does it beat the current rule and simply holding SPY? The current rule is also taken apart (2R target, 40-day limit) to see which part costs most.

variants.label: Current rule: support -5% (max 10%), sell all at 2R, 40 days
Disaster stop -50% only, sell after 60 days

notes: Account: research/backtest/account-scenario.json as approved 2026-09-08 ($100,000, 10% of initial cash per position, whole shares, at most 10 positions, 0.1% per side, no leverage, skip when the stock is held or cash or slots run out).
Same-day signals take free slots in SV score order (higher first), as live. The luck check re-runs each account 200 times with same-day order shuffled (fixed seeds).

Pass bar, approved by the user on 2026-10-08: Sharpe and Calmar both above the current rule and SPY buy-and-hold; max drawdown at most 25%; luck check median Sharpe above the current rule's and its worst 5% CAGR above zero; every five-year period positive; deflated Sharpe probability at least 0.95.
Deflated Sharpe (Bailey and Lopez de Prado 2014) counts 24 trials: the 15 rules of round 1 on this dataset plus these 9.
Trade statistics are kept as diagnostics only. Same frozen 20-year data as round 1, so a passing rule becomes a forward-test candidate, not a production rule.
SPY is also held at the same share of the account each day, to separate skill from simply being invested.
